title: Narrow-wrapped, colon-without-space and tab-escaped EC keys pass the leak scan, and the quoted EC label followed by a path is flagged
goal: The leak scan flags an EC key body wrapped under 20 characters per line, a Proc-Type header with no space after its colon and a literal tab escape separator, and does not flag the EC armor label quoted alone with a repository path on the next line

run:
import base64, os, sys, time
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import kbcommon
d = "-" * 5
arm = d + "BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY" + d
b = base64.b64encode(os.urandom(96)).decode()
hit = lambda t: any(k == "secret" for k, _ in kbcommon.leak_hits(t))
cases = {"wrap16": arm + "\n" + "\n".join(b[i:i+16] for i in range(0, 96, 16)), "hdr_nospace": arm + "\nProc-Type:4,ENCRYPTED\n" + b[:64], "tab_escape": arm + chr(92) + "t" + b[:64]}
miss = [k for k, v in cases.items() if not hit(v)]
fp = hit(arm + "\nkb/public/security/secret-shapes-in-text.md")
print("passing:", miss, "| label+path flagged:", fp)
sys.exit(1 if miss or fp else 0)

notes: Found by the SP-tsb23kev focused review of BG-3vnu37rq (reviewer session a419aba4) on origin/main 902e961a9; repro fails there.
